summary.en: The Bobcat Adventure is the first required Adventure on the trail to earn the Tiger badge of rank. Once the Bobcat Adventure is completed, Tigers can start any other of the Adventures in any order. Bobcat is focused on character and introducing the values of Scouting America.

The natural environment continues to be the best place for children to learn and discover. Being outdoors has proven benefits for both youth and adults. For Tigers, this means taking opportunities to simply take a walk outside. Tigers and adult partners will take a walk to explore the outdoors. Along the way, they can learn about domesticated and wild animals.

Personal fitness is learning about proper nutrition, hygiene, exercise, and rest. Children who develop habits at an early age are more likely to continue those habits into adulthood. In this Adventure, Tigers will explore the different food groups, have fun being active, and learn about the importance of rest.

Citizenship is one of the four aims of the Scouting America program. For Tigers citizenship begins at home and in their den. Citizenship is being part of a team. Learning that they, too, can contribute and have a part is the objective.
With world-leading experts in the field, this powerful Adventure will introduce you and your child to the Protect Yourself Rules.

In this Adventure, the Tigers learn about their family by exploring the faith traditions and celebrations that make being part of their family special. Tigers may earn this Adventure by completing the requirements for the Adventure OR by earning the religious emblem of their choosing. This Adventure is commonly done at home with the Cub Scout’s family. If it is being done as a den, ensure that every parent and guardian is aware of the content and the activities that the den will do, and allow for parents to opt out of doing it as a den activity and choose to complete the requirement at home.
Here is the opportunity for Tigers and their adult partners to go on an overnight campout.
The most popular events in Cub Scouting are found in this Adventure: the Pinewood Derby ® and the Raingutter Regatta™. Tigers and adult partners work together to build and race either a car or boat.
Astronomy is the focus of this Adventure as Tigers explore the night sky and discover constellations.

This Adventure is for the summer after a Cub Scout has completed kindergarten and is now considered a Tiger. Stay active in the summertime by attending den or pack events, Cub Scout day camp, or resident camp.

body.en: This deck contains cards to help den leaders deliver a program to complete all requirements for earning the Tiger rank. How to use this deck 1. Review the other resource cards (black border) in this deck, and review the contents. 2. Pick the Adventure you want to work on in your next den meeting. 3. Remove all cards associated with that Adventure. 4. Scan the Adventure card, and review the webpage for the Adventure you chose. Read and follow the Safety Moment for the Adventure. 5. Select one activity card for each requirement to do in your meeting. 6. Scan the QR code for each activity you selected, and follow the directions on the activity page. 7. When conducting your den meeting, have your cards on hand to use as a quick guide. Scan here for a video that shows you how to use this deck. ‣
